current_followup.result: Read-only review of current official SEC, TypeSafe, Finnhub, Reddit, and X terms confirms that source access and account credentials do not establish this project's rights to retain, display, analyze, or forward each source. SEC public EDGAR content supports a narrow reuse path subject to stated exceptions and a descriptive contact-bearing User-Agent. TypeSafe requires customer authority and input rights, consumes credits per submitted input, allows broad telemetry use, and restricts using Services or Output to develop a similar or competing product; exact account and product applicability, retention, telemetry, limits/refill, and rejected-request billing remain unverified. Finnhub terms restrict sharing data or derived results without written approval and prohibit business/internal business use of personal plans without written approval; subscription-end deletion also applies. Reddit terms limit User Content use to the app context, require a separate agreement for commercial use or other uses not expressly allowed, and restrict AI model training absent rightsholder permission. X policy restricts redistribution of content and requires removal when content is no longer available. The user-attested source-use statement is recorded separately; no endpoint-specific agreement or TypeSafe account-owner evidence has been supplied for independent review. These observations are not a legal determination.
sec_conditions: For the initial path, use public EDGAR filing content only; omit SEC marks/artwork and avoid any clearly third-party material embedded in a filing.
Configure a descriptive SEC User-Agent that identifies the operator and includes contact information; the SEC says automated tools must be classified.
Stay at or below the SEC limit of 10 requests per second aggregated across machines; the app's 125ms per-process start spacing is below this limit, but multiple processes are not coordinated.
